name: I2C Pull-up Calculator
blurb: the pull-up resistor range for an I2C bus from its supply, speed and capacitance
intro: The pull-up has to be strong enough for the bus to rise in time, and weak enough that a device can pull it low. Both limits come from the I2C specification (NXP UM10204).

inputs.label: Bus capacitance
inputs.help: About 10 pF per device plus the traces; 400 pF is the specification's limit.

inputs.label: Devices on the bus
inputs.help: Optional: what the bus capacitance is made of. The part of the bus capacitance the devices do not account for is counted as wiring.

inputs.label: Wiring capacitance
inputs.help: About 1 pF per cm of PCB trace over a ground plane; turns the wiring's capacitance into a length.

inputs.label: Chosen pull-up
inputs.help: Optional: a resistor to check instead of the suggested one, e.g. 4k7.

examples.title: Three sensors at 400 kHz on 3.3 V

usage: Give the bus supply in volts, the speed mode (standard, fast or fastplus) and the total bus capacitance in pF. It returns the minimum and maximum pull-up in ohms, a standard value between them, the rise time and sink current with that value, and a warning when no resistor can satisfy both limits (then lower the capacitance or the speed). Optionally give rp (a pull-up to check: its rise time, sink current and whether it is inside the range), devices (a list of {name, pf} pin capacitances, shown as what the bus capacitance is made of) and pfcm (wiring pF per cm).
sources: NXP UM10204 I2C-bus specification rev. 7, section 7.1 (pull-up resistor sizing) and table 10
